doc.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995

chapter: Naming the music, family and Bix
title: Playing Bix for the New York Jazz Repertory Company
summary: His first New York concert, cast as Bix Beiderbecke thanks to Pizzarelli and Davern, using Wilber's transcriptions.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Was one of your first big moments — this is something I read and I don’t know if it’s true — you did a concert with the New York Jazz Repertory and you were doing some Bix tunes or something?

Yeah, that was the first concert I really did in New York was for the New York Jazz Repertory Company, and it was the music of Bix Beiderbecke and thanks to Bucky Pizzarelli and Kenny Davern, and some very timely recommendations, I was cast as Bix for a day.
Did you do a lot of listening before that, or was it already a part of you?

I don’t — I mean I’ve been listening to you know those Beiderbecke records since I was a kid. I knew most of the stuff from having played it millions of times, just as I knew a lot of Louis Armstrong solos from having played it a hundred and — you know, a little kid with a trumpet and you hear somebody do something like “West End Blues” — it’s still pretty astounding. Even now, I’ve played the trumpet for forty years, and every time I hear “West End Blues” I think it’s astounding. So yeah, I was prepared that way, and of course Bob Wilber or somebody had done note for note transcriptions, so it was not a question of having to transcribe it myself, but rather just interpret.
He was an interesting character I guess, from what I read.
